contract: Each connection holds its own active branch and session view so two connections may use different branches of the same file
A tag-, commit-, or ancestor-qualified connection remains pinned to its immutable commit while peers advance refs and is read-only until it checks out a branch
An uncommitted working set belongs to its branch and another connection selecting that branch recovers it
An explicit write transaction owns the graph lock and a concurrent writer receives SQLITE_BUSY until the owner finishes
After the lock holder commits or exits a peer write can proceed successfully
A transaction cannot upgrade its stale read snapshot to a writer after a peer advances the store
A multiproc reader sees already-committed data while a peer holds an uncommitted write and sees the peer data after commit
An open iterator completes safely while another process runs GC
Multiprocess access does not create SQLite journal WAL or shared-memory sidecars
Two processes that commit one after another both land with consistent row counts and log history
A racing multiproc commit either advances the tip or fails busy without clobbering the peer tip
Forked SQL transaction writers leave table and index state consistent
Merge re-confirms its planned HEAD under the graph lock before advancing the branch
Cherry-pick re-confirms its planned HEAD under the graph lock before advancing the branch
A cherry-pick that loses the HEAD confirm restores session conflict state so the connection is not stuck with a phantom merge
After a cherry-pick advances the branch tip a later seal failure leaves the session on the new tip
Revert advances its planned result through the locked compare-and-advance path
Pull re-reads and compares the on-disk branch tip while holding the graph lock
Rebase uses locked branch expectations, compare-and-advance on the working tip, and rejects a concurrent peer commit without dropping peer refs
Concurrent rebase continue and abort operations claim exclusive ownership so exactly one completes successfully
HTTP push refreshes and validates plain and conditional ref installs under the graph lock so a stale refs blob cannot replace a peer update
A second connection that commits without refreshing loses to the first tip and does not overwrite it
GC reports busy or defers while a concurrent writer holds the graph lock
After the writer finishes GC completes without dropping reachable committed rows
GC racing multiproc commits leaves all committed racer rows intact
Merge racing a multiproc writer keeps feature rows and main commits reachable
Unresolved merge conflicts exist only inside the producing transaction and are never left durable on disk
